title: Box Model Lab: margin, border, padding, content dimensions
learningObjectives: Explain box model lab: margin, border, padding, content dimensions and design an accessible interactive learning lab.

understand.concept: A Box Model Lab exposes controls for content dimensions, padding, border, and margin. It should display the content box, padding area, border box, and margin area separately and calculate measurements for both content-box and border-box sizing.
understand.whyItMatters: The lab helps learners see why declared width differs from rendered outer width. Label whether measurements include margin, and keep the visual layers and numeric results synchronized.
understand.analogy: The lab is a transparent measuring frame that shows each box-model layer separately.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy supports understanding; a production lab needs real state management, safe preview isolation, and accessible controls.

explain.narrative: The starter uses distinct spacing and colours to suggest the four layers. The independent task adds live controls and numeric dimensions.

examples.explanation: The starter uses distinct spacing and colours to suggest the four layers. The independent task adds live controls and numeric dimensions.
examples.expectedOutput: A rendered starter preview for the interactive lab concept.

practise.guidedTask: Add range controls for width, padding, border width, and margin. Show content width, border-box width, and margin-inclusive occupied width; include a box-sizing switch.
practise.independentTask: Implement the lab with labelled controls, a live preview, validation, reset behaviour, and a generated CSS readout. Test keyboard and mobile operation.
hints: Keep preview state and code output synchronized.
Handle invalid input without crashing the lab.
Keep learner content isolated from the parent application.

practice.starterCode: Content
practice.resetCode: Content

questions.prompt: Which four layers must the lab display?
questions.explanation: The box model contains content, padding, border, and margin layers.

questions.prompt: What is a core quality requirement for an interactive CSS lab?
options: Accessible controls, safe validation, and synchronized output
Using innerHTML for every learner input
questions.answer: Accessible controls, safe validation, and synchronized output
questions.explanation: A learning lab must be understandable, safe, and responsive to learner input.
